w: One of the last true fragments of the primeval forest that once stretched across the whole European Plain, this UNESCO World Heritage site straddles the Poland-Belarus border and shelters more than 800 European bison - the continent's heaviest land animal - roaming old growth few other forests still have.
s: Europe's last primeval forest, and 800 wild bison
_facts: large forest complex, World Heritage Area, Poland/Belarus border
one of last and largest remaining parts of primeval forest across European Plain
home to more than 800 European bison, Europe's heaviest land animal
62km southeast of Bialystok, Poland; border crossing for hikers/cyclists

w: The strictly protected heart of Bialowieza Forest, and Poland's only natural UNESCO World Heritage Site, this park guards the best-preserved fragment of Europe's last temperate primeval forest - home to the world's largest population of European bison alongside wild boar, elk, wolf and lynx.
s: Poland's only natural World Heritage Site
_facts: national park in Podlaskie Voivodeship, adjacent to Belarus border

Poland's only natural property designated a UNESCO World Heritage Site

n: Orthodox church of the Exaltation of the Holy Cross in Narew
w: This Orthodox parish in Narew traces to the 1500s, surviving Latinization under Uniate rule before rejoining Russian Orthodoxy in 1839. Its old church was moved to the cemetery in the 1880s; a 1990 fire tore through the rebuilt interior, and icons carried off by fleeing parishioners in 1915 never came back.
s: Outlasted union, fire, and a parish's lost icons
